To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have cloned and characterized a family of small induible proteins that includes a previously described protein, macrophage inflammatory peptide, and that these proteins are members of a family of growth and inflammation factors.

a family of four small, secreted proteins, including a previously described macrophagic inflammatory protein, are expressed in activated mouse Th cells and that one of these proteins has an amino acid sequence identical to that of a protein previously shown to have a chemotactic activity for human T cells.
we have cloned a family of four related genes that are expressed more highly by activated than resting Th cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of novel genes and their products.
the identification of genes that are differentially regulated in Th cells and that may play important roles in the development of the Th cell subset phenotype.
the identification of novel T cell products that might play a role in T cell activation or T cell-mediated immunoregulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the small inducible protein (SIP) family of proteins is a new superfamily of growth, inflammatory, and activation factors that includes the macrophage inflammatory proteins, the interleukin 8 family of chemotactic proteins, and the small inducibles.

the four cDNAs isolated and described in this paper encode proteins that are part or all of the same family of small, inducable, secreted proteins that include macrophage inflammatory proteins and a variety of lymphocyte-derived factors.
the four mRNA encode four distinct proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T cell-derived small, inducble, secreted proteins (SISPs) are related to the macrophage inflammatory proteins, but the SISPs are more closely related to each other.
we have isolated and characterized cDNA encoding four small, secreted proteins expressed more abundantly by Con A-activated than by resting T lymphocytes.

the small, induible, secreted protein family is composed of at least three related proteins that are expressed in activated lymphoid cells and that one of these proteins is the macrophage inflammatory peptide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many small secreted proteins with a common structural motif, but with different functions.

there is a family of small secreted proteins that is expressed by activated lymphocytes and macrophages, but not by fibroblasts, and that this protein family may be involved in the regulation of T cell activation.
we identified a novel family of small induible proteins, including a protein expressed by Th2 cells, which are related to a family of growth and inflammation factors.
